cards.name: Accented Edges
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that finds the edges in the image and traces them with a painted line, lightly smoothing the areas between: a high Edge Brightness makes the accents read as white chalk lines, a low one as dark ink lines. Colours stay, so the result is the photo with chalky or inked painterly outlines.
use_for: chalk-outlined, sketchy poster image of a person or product
ink-outlined painterly treatment for a social graphic or comic-style panel (low Edge Brightness)
pulling shapes out of a soft, low-detail video still so they read at small sizes
textured stylised background behind a headline
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces: a wide Edge Width outlines eyes, mouth and wrinkles with heavy lines; mask faces or keep Edge Width 2-4.
Small type and logos get thick halos around every letter; keep text on a layer above the filtered one.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Clean line art with the photo removed: use Filter/Stylize/Find Edges or Filter/Stylize/Glowing Edges instead.

params.name: edgeWidth
params.does: Edge Width: width of the traced edge line; higher = heavier, blobbier outlines
params.typical: 2 default; 4-10 for a clearly visible outline

params.name: edgeBrightness
params.does: Edge Brightness: tone of the edge accents; high = white chalk lines, low = black ink lines, middle values give subtle accents

params.name: smoothness
params.does: Smoothness: how much the traced edges are smoothed; higher = fewer, cleaner edge lines with less fine detail

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("edgeWidth"), 10); d.putInteger(s("edgeBrightness"), 48); d.putInteger(s("smoothness"), 3); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("accentedEdges"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.non_destructive: yes as a Smart Filter on a smart object (general Photoshop behaviour for Filter Gallery filters, not probed by this harvest); the scripted executeAction on a plain pixel layer is destructive
cards.cost: light: 337 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; not timed at full size (1920x1080 is 16x the pixels)

review.changes: non_destructive true -> qualified string (smart-filter use not probed by the harvest; the scripted call on a pixel layer is destructive); cost: dropped the unharvested 'a few seconds at most on a full HD frame' extrapolation (full HD is 16x the 480x270 test layer and was not timed); summary/look: 'glowing' / 'glowing edges' named the sibling Filter/Stylize/Glowing Edges (which the card's own avoid offers as the alternative); now 'chalky' / 'chalk lines'. Everything else checked against the batch (keys, defaults, ranges, enum, invoke, demo in range, AI/CDR equivalents exist via pgd.py items) and left as is.

verified.note: Every edge is traced with a light chalky line and the areas between are smoothed; with Edge Brightness 48 the whole frame turns much lighter and warmer (photo mean 147 vs 106) while the colours stay.

cards.name: Angled Strokes
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that repaints the image with diagonal brush strokes, light areas stroked in one direction and dark areas in the opposite one, turning the photo into a crosswise hand-painted texture with smeared detail. Stroke Length sets the stroke size, Sharpness how crisp the strokes are, Direction Balance the mix of the two diagonals.
use_for: painterly poster or event-backdrop image from an ordinary photo
hiding blur and compression in a soft video still under visible brushwork
art-print look for a cover, invite or menu photo
brushy texture layer blended over a flat design
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces and text smear along the diagonals; mask them out or keep Stroke Length under 15.
Large images: Stroke Length tops out at 50 and does not scale with image size, so on a 4K+ file the strokes read as fine texture; work on a downsized copy.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Colour dabs instead of diagonal streaks: use Filter/Artistic/Paint Daubs or Filter/Stylize/Oil Paint.

params.name: directionBalance
params.does: Direction Balance: mix of the two stroke diagonals; 50 balances them, values toward 0 or 100 let one diagonal dominate (which end favours which diagonal was not tested here)

params.name: strokeLength
params.does: Stroke Length: length of the diagonal strokes; longer = streakier, less detail
params.typical: 15 default; 25-50 for a clearly painted look

params.name: sharpen
params.does: Sharpness: how crisp and contrasty the stroke edges are

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("directionBalance"), 50); d.putInteger(s("strokeLength"), 40); d.putInteger(s("sharpen"), 8); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("angledStrokes"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.non_destructive: yes as a Smart Filter on a smart object (general Photoshop behaviour for Filter Gallery filters, not probed by this harvest); the scripted executeAction on a plain pixel layer is destructive
cards.cost: light: 336 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; not timed at full size (1920x1080 is 16x the pixels)

review.changes: non_destructive true -> qualified string (smart-filter use not probed by the harvest; the scripted call on a pixel layer is destructive); cost: dropped the unharvested 'a few seconds at most on a full HD frame' extrapolation (full HD is 16x the 480x270 test layer and was not timed); avoid: 'Stroke Length is in pixels' was an unharvested unit; reworded to the harvested max 50. Everything else checked against the batch (keys, defaults, ranges, enum, invoke, demo in range, AI/CDR equivalents exist via pgd.py items) and left as is.

cards.name: Crosshatch
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that keeps the image's colours and detail but adds simulated pencil hatching (short diagonal strokes) and roughens the edges of the coloured areas; Strength (1-3) sets how many hatching passes are layered, so 3 gives a dense, crossed, etched texture.
use_for: hand-drawn, pencil-hatched look on a photo for an editorial illustration or poster
vintage etching or engraving-style texture that keeps the colour
giving a soft video still a crafted, textured surface
textured background for a book cover or label
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces and small type: the hatching roughens features and letter edges; mask them or keep Stroke Length under 10.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.

A monochrome pen drawing (black lines on white): use Filter/Sketch/Graphic Pen instead; CorelDRAW's Effects/Art Strokes/Pen & Ink (Crosshatch style) is expected to give monochrome ink too (its card: not render-verified), so it is not a like-for-like match.

params.name: strokeLength
params.does: Stroke Length: length of the hatching strokes

params.name: sharpen
params.does: Sharpness: how crisp and dark the hatch strokes are etched

params.name: strengthPlugin
params.does: Strength: number of hatching passes; 3 = densest crosshatching

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("strokeLength"), 30); d.putInteger(s("sharpen"), 14); d.putInteger(s("strengthPlugin"), 3); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("crosshatch"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values

cards.cost: light: 321 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; not timed at full size (1920x1080 is 16x the pixels)

cards.name: Dark Strokes
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that paints dark areas with short, tight dark strokes and light areas with long white strokes, pushing the image toward a high-contrast, moody painted look; Black Intensity and White Intensity set how far shadows go to black and lights to white.
use_for: moody, high-contrast noir painting look for a film poster or thriller cover
dramatic textured background where the shadows go inky
turning a flat, soft video still into a punchy graphic image
gritty painted texture for album art
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Dark subjects (dark suits, night shots) become solid black masses with no detail; lower Black Intensity or lighten first with Image/Adjustments/Levels.
Faces: tight dark strokes muddy skin tones; mask faces.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
A painterly result without crushed blacks: use Filter/Brush Strokes/Angled Strokes.

params.name: balance
params.does: Balance: changes the mix of stroke directions (exact behaviour not verified in this harvest; 5 is the neutral middle)

params.name: blackIntensity
params.does: Black Intensity: how strongly dark areas are pushed to black with tight strokes

params.name: whiteIntensity
params.does: White Intensity: how strongly light areas are pushed to white with long strokes

cards.name: Ink Outlines
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that redraws the image with fine, narrow dark lines over its original details in a pen-and-ink style while keeping the colours underneath; Dark Intensity darkens the inked shadow areas and Light Intensity brightens the light ones, so the photo reads as a coloured ink illustration.
use_for: comic or graphic-novel treatment of a portrait or event photo
inked illustration look for editorial and poster art
adding drawn line detail to a soft, low-detail video still
base for a hand-drawn collage, combined with Filter/Artistic/Cutout or Posterize
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
High Dark Intensity on an already dark image fills the shadows with solid black; stay under 25 on low-key photos.
Small text and fine logos get inky, broken edges; keep type on a separate layer above.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Pure black line art on white: use Filter/Sketch/Graphic Pen or Filter/Stylize/Find Edges instead.

cards.name: Spatter
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that imitates a spatter airbrush: pixels are scattered randomly within the Spray Radius, so edges turn ragged and speckled as if sprayed, while broad areas keep their colour. Low Smoothness keeps the speckles sharp and grainy; high Smoothness merges them into softer blobs.
use_for: grungy, spray-painted edges on a poster photo or title background
street-art / stencil feel for a social graphic
breaking up a clean digital look into a rough, hand-made texture
distressed edge or frame treatment applied through a layer mask
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Text and fine lines dissolve into speckle; keep type on its own layer.
Large images: Spray Radius tops out at 25 and does not scale with image size, so on 4K+ files the spatter is subtle; work on a downsized copy and scale it back up.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
A soft, even pixel scatter without the airbrush blotches: use Filter/Stylize/Diffuse.

a layer with a transparent edge: Spatter leaves the transparent edge untouched (it only roughened the type's own colour), so flatten onto a paper colour first, or apply it to a layer mask (plan runs 2026-10-15 (poster_print.grunge_distress, poster_print.torn_paper))

params.name: sprayRadius
params.does: Spray Radius: how far pixels are scattered; higher = wider, rougher spatter

params.name: smoothness
params.does: Smoothness: low = sharp, grainy speckles; high = soft, blotchy spray

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("sprayRadius"), 25); d.putInteger(s("smoothness"), 3); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("spatter"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values

cards.name: Sprayed Strokes

Its event reads back as 'separationSetup' because that stringID shares the 'SprS' code.
use_for: rain-streaked or wind-swept atmosphere on a moody poster (Vertical or a diagonal)
spray-paint / graffiti texture for a street-style graphic
directional energy or speed texture behind a headline
hiding blur and compression in a soft video still under streaky paint
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Faces and text smear into streaks; mask them out.
In scripts use the harvested event stringIDToTypeID("separationSetup") (the same ID as charIDToTypeID("SprS")); a 'sprayedStrokes' stringID was not confirmed by the harvest.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
Directional streaking that keeps the image photographic: use Filter/Blur/Motion Blur instead.

cards.name: Sumi-e
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Brush Strokes filter that paints the image in Japanese ink-brush style, as if with a wet brush full of black ink on absorbent rice paper: soft, bleeding stroke edges and rich, deep blacks, with the colours kept but darkened. Stroke Width sets the brush size, Stroke Pressure how much ink goes down, Contrast (scripting key 'center') the tonal punch.
use_for: East-Asian ink-wash style artwork for a poster, menu or festival graphic
dark, painterly portrait or event-photo treatment
turning a soft video still into a brushy ink painting
high-contrast dark texture for a book or album cover
avoid: Filter > Brush Strokes is hidden in the menu by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Dark images and dark clothing turn into solid black blobs; lower Stroke Pressure (0-3) or lighten first with Image/Adjustments/Levels.
Faces lose detail in the ink bleed; mask them.
CMYK, Lab or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert first.
A light, colour-preserving painted look: use Filter/Artistic/Watercolor instead.
